title: It's My Life
label: EMI
about: Talk Talk's second studio album, a synth-pop record made in 1983 with producer Tim Friese-Greene. Its singles included the title track, Such a Shame and Dum Dum Girl. The album sold best in continental Europe, reaching the top five in Switzerland, the Netherlands and Germany, while it peaked at 35 in the UK and 42 in the US.

title: R Is For Rocket
label: Transgressive Records
about: This is the first full-length record by the Los Angeles group Rocket, issued through Transgressive. Desi Scaglione produced it, and sessions took place at 64 Sound and Studio 606. The ten songs lean toward alternative rock, and critics rated it highly, with a Metacritic average in the low eighties.

title: Oshin
label: Captured Tracks
about: DIIV made its full-length debut with this dream pop record on Captured Tracks, and bandleader Zachary Cole Smith produced it himself. Reviews were favorable. The record went out of print for a while in 2014 over a dispute about its cover image, and it came back in 2015 with new artwork.

title: Computer Games
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Eddie Hazel, Garry Shider, Junie Morrison, Tony Thomas – guitar
Bootsy Collins, Junie Morrison – bass. Dennis Chambers, Jerry Jones – drums
Bernie Worrell, David Spradley, Junie Morrison, Rahni Harris – keyboards
Fred Wesley, Larry Hatcher, Maceo Parker, Richard Griffith – horns
about: George Clinton's first solo album came out on Capitol, although many Parliament and Funkadelic players performed on it. It reached number 3 on the R&B album chart and number 40 on the Billboard 200. Atomic Dog topped the R&B singles chart, and Loopzilla was also an R&B hit.

title: Face The Music
label: United Artists Records
personnel: Richard Tandy – piano, clavinet, Moog, guitar, piano
about: ELO's fifth studio album, produced by Jeff Lynne and recorded mainly in Munich in 1975. It moved the band toward a more radio-friendly pop-rock sound and included the hit single Evil Woman. The record reached the US top ten and earned gold certifications in the US and Canada.

title: Naughty
label: Get On Down
personnel: Jeff Mironov, Hamish Stuart, Phil Upchurch, Steve Khan – guitar
Steve Ferrone – drums. Ken Bichel – synthesizer. Arthur Jenkins – percussion
about: Chaka Khan's second solo record was produced by Arif Mardin for Warner Bros. It reached number 6 on the R&B album chart and number 43 on the Billboard 200. Clouds was among its singles, and a teenage Whitney Houston sang backing vocals on it alongside her mother, Cissy.

title: Low-Life
label: Warner Music
about: New Order's third studio album, which the band produced themselves and released on Factory Records. It moved them further toward synthesizer-driven dance rock and produced the singles The Perfect Kiss and Sub-culture. The album reached number seven in the UK, topped the UK independent chart and was well received by critics.

title: Brotherhood
label: Factory

tracks.t: As It Is When It Was

about: New Order's fourth studio album, self-produced and recorded in London, Dublin and Liverpool. The band split it loosely into a guitar-based half and an electronic half. It contains Bizarre Love Triangle, which became their breakthrough single in the US and Australia. The album reached number nine in the UK and received mostly favourable reviews.

title: Fire Of Love
label: Blixa Sounds
personnel: Jeffrey Lee Pierce – vocals, slide guitar
about: The Gun Club's debut album, released on Ruby Records. Chris D. and Tito Larriva shared the production. The album mixed punk rock with blues and other American roots music, and it is credited with helping to create punk blues. It includes Sex Beat and For the Love of Ivy, and later garage and alternative acts cited it as an influence.

title: The Tubes
label: A&M Records
personnel: Bill Spooner, Roger Steen – guitar, vocals
Michael Cotten – synthesizer. Vince Welnick- keyboards
Rick Anderson – bass. Prairie L'Emprere Prince – drums

tracks.t: What Do You Want From Life

about: The San Francisco band's first studio album, produced by Al Kooper for A&M and recorded in Los Angeles in early 1975. It contains White Punks on Dope, which later reached the UK singles top 30. Re Styles, the model on the cover, went on to sing with the group.

title: Rodrigo Y Gabriela
label: ATO Records
about: The Mexican guitar duo's second studio album, produced with John Leckie and recorded in Bath. It came out first in Ireland, where it went to number one and was certified platinum. The album includes acoustic instrumental versions of Led Zeppelin's Stairway to Heaven and Metallica's Orion.
vinylColor: Gatefold, Bonus LP re-foc, Gold Emerald & Gold Black Ice Colored Vinyl

title: Shake It Up
label: Rhino Records
personnel: David Robinson – drums. Greg Hawkes – keyboards, vocals
about: The fourth studio LP by the Cars came out on Elektra and was the last of their records produced by Roy Thomas Baker. Its sound leaned further toward pop than Panorama did. The title song gave the group its first US top-ten single, and the album reached number 9 in the US and went double platinum.

title: Eye In The Sky
label: Cooking Vinyl
personnel: Alan Parsons – keyboards, Fairlight, drum machine, vocals
Eric Woolfson – Wurlitzer, keyboards, piano, organ, vocals
Ian Bairnson – guitar. Stuart Elliott – drums
Chris Rainbow, Lenny Zakatek, Colin Blunstone, Elmer Gantry – vocals

tracks.t: You're Gonna Get Your Fingers Burned

about: The Alan Parsons Project's sixth studio album was recorded at Abbey Road and released on Arista. Its title track became the group's biggest US single. The album topped the charts in several European countries and went platinum in the US. Its instrumental opener Sirius later became a familiar sports-arena intro.

title: Kintsugi
label: Barsuk Records

tracks.t: You've Haunted Me All My Life
Good Help (Is So Hard To Find)

about: Death Cab for Cutie's eighth studio album and the first made with an outside producer, Rich Costey. It was the last album to feature guitarist Chris Walla, who announced he was leaving during the sessions. The title refers to the Japanese art of repairing pottery. It entered the Billboard 200 at number eight and received a Grammy nomination.

label: Rhino Records
personnel: Edward Van Halen – guitar, keyboards, vocals
discs: Disc 1: Original Album Remastered; Disc 2: Rarities Remastered

tracks.t: Why Can't This Be Love (Extended Version)

about: Van Halen's seventh studio album was the first to feature Sammy Hagar, who replaced David Lee Roth on vocals. It took its name from Eddie Van Halen's home studio. It was the group's first record to top the Billboard 200, its singles included Why Can't This Be Love and Dreams, and it later went six times platinum.

title: Candy-O
label: Rhino Records
personnel: Benjamin Orr – vocals, bass. David Robinson – drums
Greg Hawkes – keyboards, percussion, saxophone, vocals

tracks.t: You Can't Hold On Too Long
Got A Lot On My Head

about: The Cars followed their debut with this second record on Elektra, again produced by Roy Thomas Baker. It reached number 3 in the US and was eventually certified four times platinum. Let's Go became the band's first top-20 single. Alberto Vargas, the veteran pin-up painter, created the cover art.

title: Gish
label: Martha's Music
about: The Smashing Pumpkins' debut studio album, co-produced by Butch Vig and Billy Corgan at Smart Studios in Madison on a small budget. It is named after the silent-film star Lillian Gish. The album charted only modestly at first but led the college radio chart, and it later went platinum in the US.
vinylColor: Gray With Pink & Purple Splatter, 180 gr

title: Skin Tight
label: Elemental Music
personnel: James "Diamond" Williams – drums, chimes, percussion, vocals
Billy Beck – piano, organ, Clavinet, ARP, percussion, vocals
Ralph "Pee Wee" Middlebrooks, Clarence "Satch" Satchell – horns, vocals
Marvin "Merv" Pierce – trumpet, flugelhorn, trombone vocals

tracks.t: It's Your Night / Words Of Love

about: The Ohio Players' fifth studio album was their first for Mercury and is seen as their commercial breakthrough, moving toward a smoother, jazz-tinged funk. It topped the soul albums chart and reached number 11 on the main pop album chart. Its singles were the title track and Jive Turkey.

title: What Were Once Vices Are Now Habits
label: Warner Records
personnel: Tom Johnston, Patrick Simmons – vocals, guitar
John Hartman, Michael Hossack, Keith Knudsen – drums

tracks.t: Tell Me What You Want (And I'll Give You What You Need)

about: The Doobie Brothers' fourth studio album was produced by Ted Templeman for Warner Bros. and reached number 4 in the US. Black Water first appeared as a B-side and was later issued as a single in its own right. It became the band's first number-one hit.

title: Agent Provocateur
label: Atlantic
personnel: Mick Jones – guitars, bass, keyboards, synthesizers, backing vocals

tracks.t: I Want To Know What Love Is

about: Foreigner's fifth studio album was produced by Mick Jones and Alex Sadkin after Trevor Horn left the project early. It was the band's only UK number-one album and reached number 4 in the US. Its lead single, I Want to Know What Love Is, topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic.

title: Archive Vol. 1 (1981 - 1990)
label: Virgin
personnel: Andy McCluskey – vocals, guitar, bass, keyboards, synthesizers
Paul Humphreys – keyboards, synthesizers, vocals, percussion

title: Fantasies
label: Metric Music International
about: Metric's fourth studio album, self-released after recording sessions in New York and Ontario with producer Gavin Brown. Its singles included Help I'm Alive, Gimme Sympathy and Gold Guns Girls. The record went platinum in Canada, won the 2010 Juno for Alternative Album of the Year and made the 2009 Polaris Prize shortlist.

title: Hallucinating Love
label: Ninja Tune
personnel: Holly Walker, Andreya Triana, Gaidaa – vocals

title: I Built You A Tower
label: Anti-
about: The band's eleventh studio album and its first on Anti- after more than two decades with Atlantic. John Congleton produced it, mostly over three weeks in Los Angeles. Ben Gibbard wrote much of it after his marriage ended. Riptides was released as the lead single.

title: Money For Nothing / Greatest Hits

tracks.t: Where Do You Think You're Going

about: This greatest hits set draws on the band's first five albums, starting with Sultans of Swing. It went to number one in the UK, the Netherlands and Switzerland and gained several platinum awards. The cover is a still from the Money for Nothing video, and that song appears here without its disputed second verse.

title: Brothers In Arms
label: Warner Bros. Records
about: Dire Straits made this record in Montserrat and New York with Mark Knopfler and Neil Dorfsman producing, and Sting sings on Money for Nothing. It was recorded fully digitally and became the first album to sell a million copies on CD. It topped the UK and US charts and has sold more than 30 million copies.

title: Alchemy - Dire Straits Live (Part Two)
label: Warner Bros. Records
about: The band's first live release is a double album taken from the last two shows of the Love Over Gold tour, at London's Hammersmith Odeon in July 1983. The two-disc CD edition added Love over Gold and made several tracks longer. It reached number 3 in the UK and number 46 in the US.

title: Deep Forest / World Mix
label: Columbia
about: The French duo Éric Mouquet and Michel Sanchez blended samples of traditional singing with ambient and dance beats on their first album. It sold over 3.5 million copies and was nominated for a Grammy. A 1994 reissue called World Mix kept the original tracks and added extra mixes. Sampling disputes later took the album out of print.

title: Mixed Up
label: Elektra
about: The Cure reworked several of their earlier singles here and added one new song, Never Enough. Robert Smith was among the producers. The album went to number 8 in the UK and number 14 in the US, went platinum in America, and was followed in 2018 by a deluxe reissue and a sequel, Torn Down.

title: Woodface
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Neil Finn – guitar, vocals, keyboards, producer
Paul Hester – drums, vocals, keyboards, percussion
about: Tim Finn joined his brother Neil in the band for this album and co-wrote eight of its songs, several first planned for a Finn Brothers project. Singles included Weather with You and Fall at Your Feet. It was their first top-ten album in the UK, where it went double platinum, and it topped the New Zealand chart.

title: This Desert Life
label: DGC
personnel: Dan Vickrey – electric guitar, acoustic guitar, vocals
Charles Gillingham – mellotron, piano, electric piano, organ, synthesizer, acoustic guitar, chamberlin, vocals

tracks.t: I Wish I Was A Girl
St. Robinson In His Cadillac Dream

about: David Lowery and Dennis Herring produced the band's third album. Its lead single, Hanginaround, topped the US adult alternative chart, and Mrs. Potter's Lullaby followed. The album reached number 8 on the Billboard 200, went platinum in the US and Canada, and had sold over two million copies worldwide by early 2002.

title: Fat City
label: Columbia
about: This was Colvin's second studio record, coming after her Grammy-winning debut Steady On. Larry Klein and John Leventhal were among its several producers. Round of Blues reached the Modern Rock chart, and I Don't Know Why charted on the Adult Contemporary list.

title: Hello, I Must Be Going!
label: Atlantic

tracks.t: Do You Know, Do You Care?
Don't Let Him Steal Your Heart Away

about: Collins co-produced his second solo album with Hugh Padgham. His version of the Supremes hit You Can't Hurry Love went to number one in the UK. The album peaked at number 2 in Britain and number 8 in the US, topped the Canadian chart, and went triple platinum in both the UK and US.

title: Face Value
label: Atlantic
about: Collins wrote much of his first solo album after his first marriage ended, while Genesis were on a break. In the Air Tonight was its biggest hit and reached number 2 in the UK. The album topped the UK chart, reached number 7 in the US, and has sold about 12 million copies.

title: 24 Nights
label: Reprise Records

tracks.t: Have You Ever Loved A Woman

about: A live set from Eric Clapton, taken from his long series of Royal Albert Hall concerts in London in 1990 and 1991. Clapton played these shows with four different line-ups: a small rock band, a large band, a blues group with guests, and an orchestra conducted by Michael Kamen. An expanded box set came out in 2023.

title: Journeyman
label: Reprise Records
about: Clapton's eleventh solo studio record, produced by Russ Titelman for Duck/Reprise. Reviewers treated it as a comeback after his struggle with alcohol. It mixes polished late-1980s production with blues material. The album reached No. 2 in the UK and No. 16 in the US, and it later went double platinum in America.

title: Tracy Chapman
label: Elektra
about: The first album by singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman, issued by Elektra and produced by David Kershenbaum. It went to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and contains the hit Fast Car. Worldwide sales are estimated at more than 20 million copies.

title: His Greatest Hits Vol. 2
label: DCC Compact Classics
personnel: Ray Charles – piano, vocals, producer, remix

tracks.t: Take These Chains From My Heart
In The Heat Of The Night
Look What They Done To My Song, Ma
I Chose To Sing The Blues

title: Aglio E Olio
label: Fellaheen
about: A short hardcore punk EP that the Beastie Boys released on their Grand Royal label, going back to their punk beginnings. It collects hardcore songs that did not fit the band's next full album. The title is Italian for garlic and oil, a simple pasta dish, and it nods to how short the record is.

title: Shooting Rubberbands At The Stars
label: Geffen Records
about: The first studio album by the Texas band Edie Brickell & New Bohemians, released by Geffen and produced by Pat Moran at Rockfield Studios in Wales. Its single What I Am reached the US top ten. The album peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and went double platinum.

artist: Big Head Todd And The Monsters
title: Sister Sweetly
label: Giant Records
personnel: Brian Nevin – drums, percussion, backing vocals
Todd Park Mohr – guitar, keyboards, vocals
about: The third album by the Colorado rock group Big Head Todd and the Monsters, and their first for Giant Records. David Z produced it, and frontman Todd Park Mohr wrote all the songs. It only reached No. 117 on the Billboard 200 but still sold over a million copies and went platinum.
artistKey: Big Head Todd and the Monsters

title: Disc One: All Their Greatest Hits 1991-2001
label: Reprise Records

tracks.t: It's Only Me (The Wizard Of Magicland)

about: A Reprise Records retrospective covering the Canadian band's first ten years of singles. Alongside familiar hits, it adds two newly recorded songs, one of them the single Thanks That Was Fun, plus previously non-album tracks. It reached number 3 in Canada and number 38 in the US, earning gold status there.

title: Snacktime!
label: Desperation Records
personnel: Michael Phillip Wojewoda – vocals, percussion, producer
Ed Robertson – vocals, acoustic guitar, electric guitar, banjo, percussion
Steven Page – vocals, acoustic guitar, electric guitar, percussion
Jim Creeggan – vocals, bass guitar, cello, violin, percussion
Kevin Hearn – vocals, keyboards, guitar, mandolin, banjo, accordion, saw, percussion
about: A studio record of songs aimed at children, illustrated by keyboardist Kevin Hearn and paired with a companion book. It was the final release featuring Steven Page before his 2009 exit. The album charted at number 10 in Canada and won the 2009 Juno for Children's Album of the Year.

title: Maroon
label: Reprise Records

tracks.t: Tonight Is The Night I Fell Asleep At The Wheel

about: The band's follow-up to the hugely successful Stunt, produced by Don Was for Reprise. Its lead single Pinch Me became a top-20 US hit. The record entered the Billboard 200 at number 5, charted near the top in Canada, and went platinum in both countries.

title: Compositions
label: Elektra
about: Baker's Elektra release of 1990, her last made with producer Michael J. Powell. Led by the single Talk to Me, it climbed to number 5 on the Billboard 200 and number 3 on the R&B albums chart. It went platinum in the US and brought her a Grammy for female R&B vocal performance.

title: Giving You The Best That I Got
label: Elektra

tracks.t: Giving You The Best That I Got

about: Baker's 1988 Elektra album and the only one of her records to top the Billboard 200. Its title song became her highest-charting pop single, peaking at number 3. The album was certified triple platinum and collected multiple Grammy and Soul Train awards.

title: Neon Bible
label: Merge Records
about: Arcade Fire's second record, made largely in a converted church the band purchased in Farnham, Quebec, and issued on Merge. It opened at number 2 in the US and topped the charts in Canada and Ireland. Critics praised it widely, and it won the 2008 Juno for Alternative Album of the Year.

title: Back In Black
label: Atlantic

tracks.t: What Do You Do For Money Honey
Let Me Put My Love Into You
You Shook Me All Night Long
Rock And Roll Ain't Noise Pollution

about: AC/DC's first album with singer Brian Johnson, recorded in the Bahamas with producer Mutt Lange after Bon Scott died earlier that year. The all-black cover was a tribute to Scott. It is one of the best-selling albums of all time, with sales estimated at around 50 million, and it is a landmark of hard rock.

title: Gold (Greatest Hits)
label: Polydor

tracks.t: Lay All Your Love On Me
Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)

about: A collection of ABBA hits that PolyGram released after it bought Polar Music and the band's catalogue. It is ABBA's best-selling album, at roughly 30 million copies, and has been reissued several times. It is credited with bringing the group back into fashion a decade after they split.

title: MTV Unplugged
label: Elektra
personnel: Bill Dillon – acoustic guitar, mandolin, slide guitar
about: An acoustic concert taped in New York in April 1993 for MTV's Unplugged series and produced by Paul Fox. Singer Natalie Merchant quit the group before it came out. Its version of Because the Night became the band's biggest single, and the album eventually sold three million US copies.

title: Our Time In Eden
label: Elektra
personnel: Rob Buck – electric guitar, acoustic guitar, sitar, banjo, pedal steel guitar, lap steel guitar, mandocello
Dennis Drew – organ, piano, keyboards, accordion
about: The final studio album the band made with Natalie Merchant as lead vocalist, produced by Paul Fox for Elektra. Horn parts came from members of James Brown's backing group, and future singer Mary Ramsey appears on several songs. Singles included These Are Days and Candy Everybody Wants; it went double platinum in the US.

title: In My Tribe
label: Elektra
personnel: Robert Buck – band, guitar, mandolin, pedal steel guitar
about: The Peter Asher-produced Elektra album that gave the band its commercial breakthrough, featuring songs such as Like the Weather and What's the Matter Here. It reached number 37 in the US and went double platinum. Their Peace Train cover was removed from US pressings in 1989 after Cat Stevens' remarks about Salman Rushdie.

title: Mister Heartbreak
label: Warner Brothers
personnel: Laurie Anderson – vocals, synclavier; violin; whistle; vocoder; electronic conches; bell; percussion; artwork; graphics
Anton Fier – drums; toms, wood block
about: Laurie Anderson's second studio album, issued by Warner Bros. and co-produced with Bill Laswell, Roma Baran and Peter Gabriel. Built around the Synclavier, it features Adrian Belew on guitar and the Gabriel co-write Excellent Birds. It reached number 60 on the Billboard 200 and charted in several European countries.

title: Crush
label: Virgin Records
personnel: Paul Humphreys – vocals; electronic keyboards; piano
Andy McCluskey – vocals; guitar; bass guitar; keyboards

tracks.t: The Native Daughters Of The Golden West

about: OMD's sixth studio album and the first of two made with producer Stephen Hague, aimed largely at American listeners. It leaned on live instruments more than earlier records and yielded So in Love, Secret and La Femme Accident. It peaked at 13 in the UK and became the band's only US top-40 album.

title: Abacab
label: Atlantic Records
about: Genesis's eleventh studio album, the first recorded at their own studio, The Farm, in Surrey and the first they produced themselves, with Hugh Padgham engineering. It pushed the trio further toward concise pop-oriented songs. The record topped the UK chart, reached number seven in the US and was later certified double platinum there.

title: War
label: Island Records
personnel: The Edge – Guitar, Piano, Lap Steel Guitar
about: U2's third studio album, produced by Steve Lillywhite for Island Records and widely seen as their first openly political record. Its singles included New Year's Day, Two Hearts Beat as One and Sunday Bloody Sunday. It replaced Thriller at the top of the UK chart, giving the band their first British number-one album.

title: Achtung Baby
label: Island Records

tracks.t: Even Better Than The Real Thing
Until The End Of The World
Who's Gonna Ride Your Wild Horses
Tryin' To Throw Your Arms Around The World

about: U2's seventh studio album, produced by Daniel Lanois and Brian Eno, which reinvented the band's sound with industrial, alternative and electronic dance elements after Rattle and Hum. Singles included The Fly, Mysterious Ways and One. It debuted at number one in the US, won a Grammy and has sold around 18 million copies.

title: Unplugged 1991
label: Rhino Records
personnel: Mike Mills – bass guitar, vocals, organ

tracks.t: It's The End Of The World As We Know It (And I Feel Fine)

about: Recording of R.E.M.'s 1991 MTV Unplugged acoustic performance, taped at Chelsea Studios in New York, issued by Rhino in 2014 as part of the Unplugged complete-sessions project that debuted on Record Store Day. The release included songs that had not aired in the original broadcast and was well received by critics.

title: September in the Rain
label: Mercury

tracks.t: As Long As I'm In Your Arms
With A Song In My Heart
I Can't Believe That You're In Love With Me
I Was Telling Him About You
I've Got My Love To Keep Me Warm

about: A Mercury LP by Dinah Washington blending jazz and rhythm and blues. Its title song became a hit single, reaching number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 5 on the R&B chart. The album itself entered the Billboard LP chart in late 1961 and peaked at number 56.

title: Soul Shoutin'
label: Prestige Records
personnel: Stanley Turrentine – tenor saxophone Earl May – bass

tracks.t: In The Still Of The Night

about: A Prestige jazz album by organist Shirley Scott featuring her then-husband, tenor saxophonist Stanley Turrentine. It was recorded at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in New Jersey in October 1963 with Ozzie Cadena producing, and appeared the following year. It was later reissued on CD paired with The Soul Is Willing.

title: The Magic Whip
label: Parlophone
personnel: Damon Albarn – vocals, keyboards, synthesizers, iPad, acoustic guitar
Dave Rowntree – drums, percussion, backing vocals

tracks.t: There Are Too Many Of Us

about: Blur's eighth studio album and their first in twelve years, rooted in sessions the band held in Hong Kong in 2013 after a Japanese festival date fell through. Produced with Stephen Street, it was the first album by the original four-piece since 13. It entered the UK chart at number one.

title: Violator
label: Mute Records
about: Depeche Mode's seventh studio album and their first produced with Flood, released on Mute in Britain and Sire/Reprise in the US. It contains Personal Jesus, Enjoy the Silence, Policy of Truth and World in My Eyes. It reached number two in the UK and became the band's first US top-ten and million-selling album.

title: The Idea of Beautiful
label: It's a Wonderful World Music Group
personnel: Marianna Evans (Rapsody) Guest appearances from Big Rube, Raheem DeVaughn, Ab-Soul, Mac Miller, The Cool Kids, Buckshot, Childish Gambino, GQ, Big Remo, Heather Victoria, Rocki Evans, BJ the Chicago Kid, and Nomsa Mazwai

tracks.t: Believe Me (Ha Ha Ha Ha Remix) (Bonus)

about: North Carolina rapper Rapsody's first studio album, produced mainly by 9th Wonder's Soul Council team and issued through Jamla. Guests include Mac Miller, Ab-Soul, Childish Gambino, Raheem DeVaughn and BJ the Chicago Kid. It arrived after several mixtapes and an EP, with Believe Me as the lead single.

title: Strangeways, Here We Come
label: Rhino Records
personnel: Morrissey (Steven Patrick Morrissey) – vocals, piano, cover art, handclaps
Johnny Marr – guitar, piano, keyboards, harmonica, marimba, vocals

tracks.t: A Rush And A Push And The Land Is Ours
I Started Something I Couldn't Finish
Stop Me If You Think You've Heard This One Before
Last Night I Dreamt That Somebody Loved Me

about: The Smiths' fourth and last studio album, recorded in Bath in spring 1987 and released by Rough Trade after the band had already split following Johnny Marr's departure. Singles included Girlfriend in a Coma and I Started Something I Couldn't Finish. It reached number two in the UK and went gold in Britain and the US.

title: Very Mercenary
label: Ninja Tune
personnel: Andy Hamill – double bass. with guests Roots Manuba, What What, Bahamadia Goldrush, Blade, Dream Warriors
about: The Herbaliser's third studio album, released on Ninja Tune and produced by Jake Wherry and Ollie Teeba. It mixes jazz-funk and hip hop with a spy-film flavour and features rappers including Bahamadia, Roots Manuva, What What and the Dream Warriors. It peaked at 19 on the UK independent albums chart.

title: Parallel Lines
label: Chrysalis
personnel: Jimmy Destri – electronic keyboards Nigel Harrison – bass guitar

tracks.t: I Know But I Don't Know

about: Blondie's third studio album, produced by Mike Chapman for Chrysalis and recorded in roughly six weeks. It includes Heart of Glass, Hanging on the Telephone, Sunday Girl and One Way or Another. It topped the UK chart and was Britain's best-selling album of 1979, and it entered the National Recording Registry in 2024.

title: Quiet Fire
label: Atlantic Records

tracks.t: Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow

about: Roberta Flack's third studio album, produced by Joel Dorn for Atlantic and recorded in New York. Mixing soul and gospel, it includes her version of Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow. The record reached number 18 on the Billboard 200 and number four on the R&B albums chart, and it was certified gold.

title: Pet Sounds
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Brian Wilson – vocals; producer; plucked piano strings; bass guitar, Danelectro bass, and organ; piano
Carl Wilson – vocals; lead guitar; 12-string electric guitar

tracks.t: Don't Talk (Put Your Head On My Shoulder)
I Just Wasn't Made For These Times

about: The Beach Boys' eleventh studio album, produced by Brian Wilson for Capitol with heavy use of session players such as the Wrecking Crew. It includes Wouldn't It Be Nice, God Only Knows, Sloop John B and Caroline, No. It reached number two in Britain and is now ranked among the most influential albums ever made.

title: The Bitch is Black
label: Motown Records

tracks.t: Funky Music Sho Nuff Turns Me On
It's Bad For Me To See You
I Know (You Don't Love Me No More)
Walk Out The Door If You Wanna
You Can't Judge A Book By It's Cover

about: The only album by soul singer Yvonne Fair, released on Motown and drawing on recordings made between 1972 and 1975 with producers including Norman Whitfield. It contains her UK top-five hit It Should Have Been Me. The record sold poorly at home, peaking at 57 on the R&B chart, but did better in Britain and Australia.

title: Caravanserai
label: Columbia Records

tracks.t: Look Up (To See What's Coming Down)
Just In Time To See The Sun
All The Love Of The Universe

about: Santana's fourth studio album, produced by Carlos Santana and drummer Michael Shrieve for Columbia. It moved the group toward largely instrumental jazz fusion and was the last record with several founding members. Despite label doubts about its commercial appeal, it reached number eight in the US and eventually went platinum.

title: Somebody's Been Sleeping in My Bed
label: Hot Wax Records
personnel: Steve Mancha Joe Stubbs Eddie Holiday

tracks.t: Love Is Sweeter (The Second Time Around)
One Man's Leftovers (Is Another Man's Feast)
Ain't That Lovin' You (For More Reasons Than One)
Age Ain't Nothing But A Number
I Can't Sit And Wait (Til Johnny Comes Marching Home)

about: The first LP by Detroit soul group 100 Proof (Aged in Soul), issued on Holland-Dozier-Holland's Hot Wax label. It is built around their million-selling hit Somebody's Been Sleeping, a top-ten pop single, and also includes Too Many Cooks (Spoil the Soup) and One Man's Leftovers.

title: Maggot Brain
label: Westbound Records

tracks.t: You And Your Folks, Me And My Folks

about: Funkadelic's third studio album, produced by George Clinton for Westbound. Its title track is a roughly ten-minute guitar showcase by Eddie Hazel, and it was the final album by the original lineup. It reached the top 20 of the R&B albums chart and is now ranked among the greatest albums of all time.

title: Untitled (Black Is)
label: Forever Living Originals
personnel: Kadeem Clarke. Dean Josiah "Inflo" Cover Cleopatra "Cleo Sol" Nikolic. Melisa "Kid Sister" Young Michael Kiwanuka. Laurette Josiah

tracks.t: Why We Cry Why We Die

about: Sault's third studio album, produced by Inflo and released as a free download in June 2020, with later sales benefiting charity. It addresses Black identity and struggle and includes Wildfires. Critics acclaimed it, and NPR and BBC 6 Music each named it their album of the year.

label: Forever Living Originals
personnel: Kadeem Clarke. Dean Josiah "Inflo" Cover Cleopatra "Cleo Sol" Nikolic. Melisa "Kid Sister" Young
about: The first studio album by the anonymous British collective Sault, released on Forever Living Originals and produced by Inflo and Tom Campbell. Its sound blends funk, soul and post-punk grooves. It drew strong reviews, including five stars from The Guardian, and placed high on several best-of-2019 lists.

label: Forever Living Originals
personnel: Kadeem Clarke. Dean Josiah "Inflo" Cover Cleopatra "Cleo Sol" Nikolic. Melisa "Kid Sister" Young
about: Sault's second studio album, released about four months after their debut on Forever Living Originals with Inflo producing. The ten tracks mix dance rhythms with deep soul and rhythm and blues. It received five-star reviews from The Guardian and The Arts Desk and ranked among Bandcamp's top albums of 2019.

title: That's the Way of the World
label: Columbia Records

tracks.t: That's The Way Of The World

about: Earth, Wind & Fire's sixth studio album, produced by Maurice White and Charles Stepney and also used as the soundtrack to a 1975 film of the same name. It topped the Billboard 200 and soul charts, with Shining Star reaching number one and winning a Grammy. It went triple platinum and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.

title: Sings Ballads – Blues
label: Elektra Records

tracks.t: Woman Sure Is A Curious Critter

about: A 1957 Elektra LP on which folk and blues singer Josh White performs a dozen songs to his own guitar, with bassist Al Hall and drummer Sonny Greer. The program mixes traditional material such as Midnight Special with torch and cabaret pieces like Gloomy Sunday and Miss Otis Regrets.

title: A Day in the Life
label: A&M Records

tracks.t: When A Man Loves A Woman

about: The first of Wes Montgomery's records for Creed Taylor's A&M/CTI line, cut at Van Gelder Studio in June 1967 with orchestral arrangements by Don Sebesky. It recasts pop hits, including two Beatles songs and Windy, in a jazz setting. The album topped Billboard's jazz chart and reached number 13 on the main albums chart.

title: The Songs of Rodgers and Hart
label: Jazztone

tracks.t: Give It Back To The Indians

about: Lee Wiley's songbook of Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart material for the Boston label Storyville, recorded with a small group including trumpeter Ruby Braff and pianist Jimmy Jones. It revisited a composer team she had first documented in a 1940 album set, and Storyville later reissued the sessions in longer LP form.

title: Eldorado - A Symphony by ELO
label: United Artists Records
personnel: Jeff Lynne – vocals, guitar, bass, Moog
Richard Tandy – piano, Moog, clavinet, Wurlitzer, guitar, backing vocals
Mike de Albuquerque – bass & backing vocals

tracks.t: Can't Get It Out Of My Head

about: ELO's fourth studio album and their first full concept record, following a daydreaming man who escapes ordinary life into fantasy worlds. Produced by Jeff Lynne with a real orchestra and choir, it yielded the single Can't Get It Out of My Head and became the band's first gold album in the US, peaking at 16.

title: Quarters to Dollars
label: Allied Productions
personnel: Jimmy Destri – Farfisa organ, piano, synthesizer
about: An unofficial bootleg LP gathering early Blondie recordings from the band's pre-fame period. It was not issued or authorized by the group or its labels, so its contents and pressing details are poorly documented.

title: Tapestry
label: Ode Records
personnel: James Taylor – acoustic guitar, backing vocals
Joni Mitchell – backing vocals Curtis Amy – flute; baritone, saxophone; string quartet

tracks.t: (You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman

about: Carole King's second solo album, produced by Lou Adler, which held the top of the Billboard 200 for 15 straight weeks. Its double-sided single It's Too Late and I Feel the Earth Move went to number one, and the record won four Grammys including Album of the Year. It was added to the National Recording Registry in 2003.

title: Completely Well
label: Bluesway Records
personnel: B.B. King: Vocals, lead guitar. Hugh McCracken: Rhythm guitar Paul Harris: organ, acoustic and Fender Rhodes electric piano Jerry Jemmott: Bass. Herbie Lovelle: Drums. Bert "Super Charts" DeCoteaux: string and horn arrangements
about: A B.B. King studio album for BluesWay, recorded in New York in June 1969 under producer Bill Szymczyk. Its version of The Thrill Is Gone, enhanced with strings, became a top 15 pop hit and won a Grammy. The album reached number 38 on the Billboard 200 and number 5 on the R&B albums chart.

title: Indelibly Stamped
label: A&M Records
personnel: Rick Davies – piano, Wurlitzer, Hammond organ, lead vocals, harmonica
Roger Hodgson – guitar, bass, backing vocals
Dave Winthrop – flute, saxophones, lead vocals (Track 6)
Frank Farrell – bass, piano, accordion, backing vocals
about: Supertramp's second album, self-produced after a lineup overhaul that brought in Kevin Currie and Frank Farrell. It leaned toward a harder, more straightforward rock sound than their debut and sold poorly on release, though it later earned gold certifications in France and Canada. It was Roger Hodgson's final album playing bass for the group.

title: Portfolio of Ahmad Jamal
label: Argo
personnel: Ahmad Jamal – piano Israel Crosby – double bass Vernel Fournier – drums

tracks.t: You Don't Know What Love Is
I Didn't Know What Time It Was
So Beats My Heart For You

about: A double LP on Argo capturing Ahmad Jamal's trio with bassist Israel Crosby and drummer Vernel Fournier at the Spotlite Club in Washington, D.C., in September 1958. The same engagement supplied material for another Jamal release, and the full shows appeared on CD in 2007. Keith Jarrett has cited the album as a formative influence.

title: Bad Co
label: Swan Song
personnel: Paul Rodgers – vocals, guitar, piano, tambourine
about: The first album by the British supergroup Bad Company, recorded at Headley Grange in late 1973 and issued on Island in the UK and Led Zeppelin's Swan Song label in the US. It reached number one in America on the strength of Can't Get Enough and Movin' On, and it has been certified five times platinum there.

title: Ill Communication
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Adam "Ad-Rock" Horovitz – vocals, guitar Michael "Mike D" Diamond – vocals, drums Adam "MCA" Yauch – vocals, electric bass, string bass

tracks.t: B-Boys Makin' With The Freak Freak

about: The Beastie Boys' fourth album, co-produced by the trio with Mario Caldato Jr., mixing hip hop, hardcore punk and jazz-funk instrumentals. It debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and spawned Sabotage, known for its Spike Jonze video, and Sure Shot. The record went triple platinum in the US.

title: Electric Circus
label: MCA/Geffen Records
personnel: Common (Lonnie Rashid Lynn), with: Mary J. Blige, Erykah Badu, The Neptunes, Lætitia Sadier (of Stereolab), Cee- Lo Green, J Dilla, Bilal and Jill Scott
about: Common's fifth album, his last for MCA, recorded at Electric Lady Studios with Questlove as executive producer and the Soulquarians collective. It pushed into psychedelic rock, electronic and neo soul territory, splitting critics and selling modestly. Its single Come Close featured Mary J. Blige, and later assessments have treated the album as ahead of its time.

title: Elton John
label: Uni Records
personnel: Elton John – piano, vocals, harpsichord Alan Weighall – bass

tracks.t: I Need You To Turn To

about: Elton John's second album and his first with producer Gus Dudgeon, with orchestral arrangements by Paul Buckmaster, recorded at Trident Studios in January 1970. It contained Your Song and Border Song and became his breakthrough, reaching the top five in the UK and US. It earned a Grammy nomination for Album of the Year.

title: Motherlode
label: Polydor Records Polydor
personnel: James Brown – vocals. "Sweet" Charles Sherrell, William "Bootsy" Collins, Fred Thomas – bass. Clyde Stubblefield, John "Jabo" Starks, Melvin Parker – drums. Alfonzo Kellum, Hearlon "Cheese" Martin, Jimmy Nolen – guitar

tracks.t: You Got To Have A Mother For Me
People Get Up And Drive Your Funky Soul (Remix)
I Got Ants In My Pants (Remix)

about: A Polydor collection of James Brown funk recordings from the late 1960s and early 1970s, compiled with Tim Rogers and Cliff White as a follow-up to In the Jungle Groove. Most tracks were previously unreleased studio cuts, alongside live takes and remixes. A remastered reissue with extra tracks appeared in 2003.

title: The Beatles (White Album)
label: Capitol Records
personnel: John Lennon, Paul McCartney – vocals; guitar; bass; piano; organ
George Harrison – vocals; guitar; bass; organ

tracks.t: The Continuing Story Of Bungalow Bill
Why Don't We Do It In The Road?
Everybody's Got Something To Hide Except Me And My Monkey

about: The Beatles' only double album, widely called the White Album for its plain sleeve, recorded mostly at Abbey Road between May and October 1968. Many songs were written during the band's stay in Rishikesh, India, and the set ranges across rock, folk and pop. It topped the charts in both the UK and US.

title: Promises, Promises
label: Scepter Records
personnel: Dionne Warwick – vocals Burt Bacharach, Don Sebesky, Peter Matz – arrangements

tracks.t: This Girl Is In Love With You
Whoever You Are, I Love You

about: Dionne Warwick's eleventh studio album, produced by Burt Bacharach and Hal David, built around the title song of their Broadway musical. It also featured her hit version of This Girl's in Love with You. The record reached number 18 on Billboard's pop albums chart and number 7 on the R&B albums list.

title: Brave New World
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Steve Miller – guitar, lead vocals, harmonica

tracks.t: Can't You Hear Your Daddy's Heartbeat

about: The Steve Miller Band's third album, produced by Glyn Johns and Miller and recorded in Hollywood and London after Boz Scaggs and Jim Peterman left. Paul McCartney, credited under a pseudonym, played on My Dark Hour, and Nicky Hopkins added keyboards. It peaked at number 22 on the Billboard 200.

title: Misterioso (Recorded on Tour)
label: Columbia Records
about: A Columbia album of concert recordings made at several stops on Thelonious Monk's tours, produced by Teo Macero. Tenor saxophonist Charlie Rouse joins Monk throughout, with two different bass and drum pairings across the tracks. The set mixes Monk originals such as Evidence and Bemsha Swing with standards.

title: The Long Run
label: Asylum Records
personnel: Glenn Frey, Joe Walsh – guitars, keyboards, vocals

tracks.t: The Greeks Don't Want No Freaks

about: The Eagles' sixth album and their last studio release before their 1980 split, made over roughly 18 months with producer Bill Szymczyk. It was the first to feature bassist Timothy B. Schmit. The album spent nine weeks at number one in the US and included Heartache Tonight, which won a Grammy, plus two other top ten singles.

title: That's Life
label: Legacy

tracks.t: Nice Work If You Can Get It
I've Got You Under My Skin
You Make Me Feel So Young
In The Wee Small Hours Of The Morning

about: Willie Nelson's second album of Frank Sinatra songs, following My Way from 2018, produced by Buddy Cannon and Matt Rollings for Legacy Recordings. It reached number 58 on the Billboard 200 and drew favorable reviews. The record received a Grammy nomination for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album.

title: We Are
label: Verve Records
personnel: Jon Batiste – Fender jazz bass, keyboards, mellotron, moog bass, piano, strings, theremin, vocals
Trombone Shorty – trombone. David Gauthier, Braedon Gautier, Brennan Gautier, Gospel Soul Children, Austin Rowe, Zadie Smith, PJ Morton – vocals
Cory Wong – guitar. St. Augustine High School Marching 100, Hot 8 Brass Band – brass band
about: Jon Batiste's sixth studio album, issued on Verve and produced by Batiste with Kizzo and David Pimentel, blending soul, R&B, jazz, gospel and hip hop. It peaked at number 25 on the Billboard 200. The album won Album of the Year at the 2022 Grammy Awards.

title: Untitled (Rise)
label: Forever Living Originals
personnel: Kadeem Clarke Dean Josiah "Inflo" Cover Cleopatra "Cleo Sol" Nikolic Melisa Young
about: The fourth album by the anonymous British collective Sault, produced by Inflo and released on Forever Living Originals a few months after Untitled (Black Is). Its songs respond to the 2020 protests and Black experience in Britain and America over grooves drawing on disco, boogie and Brazilian rhythms. It was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize.

title: Stamp Out Reality
label: Melting Pot Music

tracks.t: It Was A Very Good Year

about: A collaborative album by Berlin DJ and producer Marc Hype and pianist Jim Dunloop, released in 2009 on Melting Pot Music. It extends their partnership of live piano played over funk breaks and hip hop beats, which they had developed in DJ sets and a run of singles from 2005 onward.

title: Special Beat Service
label: I.R.S. Records
personnel: Ranking Roger – Toasting, vocals, percussion Dave Wakeling – Vocals, guitar David Steele – Bass, banjo
Andy Cox – Guitar, mandolin Everett Morton – Drums

tracks.t: Pato And Roger A Go Talk

about: The third and final album of the Beat's original run, produced by Bob Sargeant and issued in North America under the name the English Beat. It broadened their ska sound toward pop and new wave and included Save It for Later, Jeanette and I Confess. It peaked at 21 in the UK and 39 in the US.

title: Missing Persons
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Terry Bozzio – vocals, keyboards, synthesizers, drums
Warren Cuccurullo – guitar, vocals Patrick O'Hearn – electric & synthesized bass, keyboards, synthesizers Chuck Wild – synthesizer, keyboard
about: This short self-titled record was the band's first release, cut at Frank Zappa's home studio with money from Warren Cuccurullo's father and first sold by the group itself. Once Missing Persons signed with Capitol in 1982, the label reissued it with Words in place of a Doors cover, and that version sold far more widely.

title: After Bathing at Baxter's
label: RCA Victor
personnel: Grace Slick – piano, organ, recorder, vocals
Jorma Kaukonen – lead guitar, sitar, vocals

tracks.t: The Ballad Of You & Me & Pooneil
A Small Package Of Value Will Come To You Shortly
The Last Wall Of The Castle

about: Jefferson Airplane's third LP was produced by Al Schmitt for RCA Victor and recorded in Hollywood. It was a far more experimental and costly project than Surrealistic Pillow, with a budget roughly ten times larger. Ron Cobb drew the cover, and the record peaked at number 17 on the Billboard 200.

title: It's a Beautiful Day
label: Columbia Records
personnel: David LaFlamme – violin, flute, lead vocals Linda LaFlamme – acoustic piano, electric piano, organ, celeste, harpsichord Hal Wagenet – guitars
about: The San Francisco group's first LP came out on Columbia with violinist David LaFlamme producing. It opens with White Bird, the band's best-known song, and spent 70 weeks on the Billboard 200, reaching number 47 and later going gold. Its painted cover is often ranked among rock's finest album sleeves.

title: Cheap Thrills
label: CBS
personnel: Janis Joplin – vocals Sam Andrew – guitar, vocals
James Gurley – guitar Peter Albin – bass, guitar

tracks.t: I Need A Man To Love

about: The band's second LP, and Janis Joplin's last with them, was produced by John Simon for Columbia. It held the top spot on the Billboard album chart for eight weeks and featured the hit Piece of My Heart. Only Ball and Chain was truly live; crowd noise was added elsewhere. Robert Crumb drew the cover.

title: Taylored in Silk
label: Stax Records

tracks.t: We're Getting Careless With Our Love
I Believe In You (You Believe In Me)
One Thing Wrong With My Woman
I Can Read Between The Lines

about: Johnnie Taylor made this Stax album with producer Don Davis, using the Muscle Shoals rhythm section and string arrangements by Wade Marcus. It contains I Believe in You (You Believe in Me), which topped the soul singles chart, plus Cheaper to Keep Her and a reading of the Dinah Washington standard This Bitter Earth.

title: Live at Carnegie Hall
label: United Artists Records
personnel: Woody Herman & The Young Thundering Herd – orchestra

tracks.t: Goldfinger (From the United Artists Motion Picture)
Where Am I Going (From the musical production "Sweet Charity")
Let Me Sing And I'm Happy
For All We Know (From The Motion Picture "Love And Other Strangers")
I'd Like To Hate Myself In The Morning
Day By Day (From The Musical Production "Godspell")
Diamonds Are Forever (From The United Artists Motion Picture)
Big Spender (From The Musical Production "Sweet Charity")
You And I (From The Mgm Motion Picture "Goodbye Mr. Chips")
A Lovely Way To Spend An Evening (Shirley Bassey Acknowledging Audience Applause)
A Lovely Way To Spend An Evening (Shirley Bassey Acknowledging Audience Applause)

about: A double LP on United Artists capturing the Welsh singer in concert at the famous New York venue. It did not chart in Britain, but in the United States it reached number 136 on the main album chart and number 20 on the R&B album chart.

title: Licensed to Ill
label: Def Jam Recordings
about: The Beastie Boys' first album was produced by Rick Rubin and issued through Def Jam and Columbia. Mixing hip hop with hard rock, it became the first rap LP to top the Billboard 200 and eventually earned diamond certification in the US. Singles included Brass Monkey and (You Gotta) Fight for Your Right.

title: Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
label: RCA

tracks.t: Can It Be All So Simple
Wu-Tang Clan Ain't Nuthing Ta F' Wit

about: The Staten Island collective's first album was produced entirely by RZA and released through Loud and RCA. Its gritty, kung fu film inspired sound and the interplay of its many rappers made it a landmark of East Coast hip hop. It reached number 41 on the Billboard 200 and launched several solo careers.

title: This is How It Is
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Ski Betz (David Anthony Willis) Suave Lover
about: Original Flavor's first album was released by Atlantic and produced by group member Ski. It was recorded in Brooklyn and Manhattan during 1991 and 1992 and runs thirteen tracks. The duo followed it with Beyond Flavor in 1994.

title: Love Ya / What Am I Fighting For? (remixes)
label: Virgin Records
personnel: Tendai Tyson Bobby Joel Stearns Adonistar

tracks.t: What Am I Fighting For? (Elektrons Data Transfer)
What Am I Fighting For? (Elektrons Data Transfer Dub)

about: A 12-inch promotional pressing pairing remixes of UnkleJam's first two singles, Love Ya and What Am I Fighting For?, both released on Virgin in 2007. The latter, written with Mike Spencer, peaked at number 16 on the UK singles chart.

title: Pushin On
label: Ubiquity
personnel: William Holland – saxaphone, tambourine, sitar, organ, percussion
about: The second album from Will Holland's funk and soul ensemble came out on Tru Thoughts in Britain and Ubiquity in the US. Singer Alice Russell appears on several songs. The title track later turned up in the first episode of the TV series Californication.

title: Enta Da Stage
label: Wreck Records
about: Black Moon's first album was released by Nervous Records and produced by Da Beatminerz, whose dark, jazzy beats shaped its sound. It reached number 33 on the R&B/hip hop album chart, and singles such as Who Got da Props?, I Got Cha Opin and Buck Em Down kept the Brooklyn trio on rap radio.

title: The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway
label: Atco Records
personnel: Phil Collins – drums, percussion, vibraphone, backing vocals

tracks.t: The Lamb Lies Down On Broadway
The Grand Parade Of LIfeless Packaging
The Light Dies Down On Broadway

about: This double concept album follows Rael, a young New Yorker drawn into a strange underground world, on a surreal journey of self-discovery. Issued on Charisma, it was the last Genesis studio album with Peter Gabriel, who left after the tour. It reached number 10 in the UK and number 41 in the US.

title: Volunteers
label: RCA Victor
personnel: Grace Slick – vocals, piano, organ, recorder
about: Jefferson Airplane's fifth LP, again produced by Al Schmitt for RCA, was recorded in San Francisco and stirred controversy with its anti-war politics and profanity. It reached number 13 in the US and went gold quickly. It was the final album with Marty Balin and Spencer Dryden.

title: Hotcakes
label: Elektra Records

tracks.t: Think I'm Gonna Have A Baby
Haven't Got Time For The Pain

about: Carly Simon's fourth album was produced by Richard Perry for Elektra. It includes Mockingbird, her duet with then husband James Taylor, and Haven't Got Time for the Pain. The record climbed to number 3 on the Billboard 200 and was certified gold.

title: Full Circle (Instrumentals)
label: Hiero Imperium
about: An instrumental edition of Full Circle, the Oakland crew's second group album from 2003, which was produced in-house by Domino, Opio, A-Plus, Casual and others and released on their own Hieroglyphics Imperium label. This version presents the beats without the vocals.

artist: Nicky Hopkins, Ry Cooder, Mick Jagger, Bill Wyman, Charlie Watts
title: Jamming With Edward!
label: Rolling Stones Records
personnel: Nicky Hopkins – keyboards, piano Bill Wyman – bass guitar

tracks.t: The Loveliest Night Of The Year

about: These loose jams were taped at Olympic Studios in London in April 1969, during the Let It Bleed sessions, while the musicians waited for an absent Keith Richards. Released on Rolling Stones Records, the set reached number 33 in the US. Edward was a nickname for pianist Nicky Hopkins.
artistKey: Nicky Hopkins, Ry Cooder, Mick Jagger, Bill Wyman, Charlie Watts

title: Late For The Sky
label: Asylum Records
personnel: Dan Fogelberg, Don Henley – harmony vocals
Doug Haywood – bass guitar, harmony vocals
about: Jackson Browne's third album, released on Asylum and co-produced with Al Schmitt, features David Lindley prominently on guitar and fiddle. Its cover photo was modeled on a Magritte painting. The record peaked at number 14 in both the US and Canada.

title: The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
label: Ruffhouse Records

tracks.t: Can't Take My Eyes Off Of You

about: Lauryn Hill's only solo studio album, released by Ruffhouse and Columbia, blends hip hop, soul and reggae. It debuted at number one in the US and won five Grammys, including Album of the Year. Singles included Doo Wop (That Thing) and Ex-Factor, and it has sold well over 20 million copies worldwide.

title: America
label: Warner Bros Records
personnel: Dewey Bunnell – lead and backing vocals, guitar
Gerry Beckley – bass, guitar, lead and backing vocals, chimes
Dan Peek – guitar, lead and backing vocals, piano, bass
about: The trio's first album appeared on Warner Bros. with Ian Samwell producing. It was initially issued without A Horse with No Name, which was added in early 1972 after the song became a worldwide hit. The album then spent five weeks at number one in the US and went platinum.

title: Fulfillingness' First Finale
label: Tamla Records

tracks.t: Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away
They Won't Go When I Go

about: Released on Motown's Tamla label, this album topped the US pop album chart and held the soul album chart for eight weeks. You Haven't Done Nothin' became a number-one single, and Boogie On Reggae Woman was also a hit. It won three Grammys, including Album of the Year.

title: Paradise Moods
label: Sunset Records
about: An exotica LP issued on Liberty's budget imprint Sunset, offering lush instrumental versions of standards such as Temptation, Siboney and Singin' in the Rain alongside several Martin Denny originals and a Debussy piece.

title: Waiter, Make Mine Blues
label: Verve Records
personnel: Anita O'Day - vocals Russell Garcia - arranger
about: Anita O'Day recorded this vocal jazz set in Los Angeles in 1960 with arrangements by Russell Garcia, and Verve released it the following year. The supporting band featured Bud Shank on saxophone and flute and Barney Kessel on guitar.

title: Let's Play
label: Imperial Records

tracks.t: When The Saints Go Marching In
I'm Gonna Be A Wheel Some Day
I Want To Walk You Home

about: Fats Domino's seventh album was released by Imperial and produced by his longtime partner Dave Bartholomew. Its twelve songs, mostly written by the pair, showcase the New Orleans rhythm and blues sound that made Domino a rock and roll star.

title: Like Water for Chocolate
label: Geffen Records

tracks.t: Pops Rap III... All My Children

about: Common's fourth studio album came out on MCA in 2000, with much of the production handled by J Dilla alongside Questlove and other Soulquarians collaborators. It featured the Grammy-nominated single The Light, reached No. 16 on the Billboard 200 and went gold, and is widely regarded as one of his strongest records.

title: Boys in the Trees
label: Elektra Records
about: Carly Simon's seventh studio album was produced by Arif Mardin and issued by Elektra in 1978. It yielded the top-ten hit You Belong to Me and a duet with James Taylor on Devoted to You, sold over a million copies in the US, and its packaging won a Grammy.

title: Energy
label: Planet Records
personnel: Anita Pointer – lead vocals, tambourine Ruth Pointer – lead vocals June Pointer – lead vocals
about: The Pointer Sisters' fifth studio album, released on Planet in 1978, was their first project with producer Richard Perry and moved them toward pop and rock material. Its cover of Bruce Springsteen's Fire reached No. 2 in the US, and the record went gold.

title: Loverboy
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Paul Dean – guitar, backing vocals Doug Johnson – keyboards
Scott Smith – bass Matt Frenette – drums
about: Loverboy's self-titled debut, produced by Bruce Fairbairn, appeared in Canada in mid-1980 and in the US that November. Driven by the single Turn Me Loose, it became a major hit at home, eventually earning seven-times platinum status in Canada and double platinum in the United States.

title: Bayou Country
label: Fantasy Records
personnel: John Fogerty – lead guitar, vocals, harmonica, piano, percussion
Tom Fogerty – backing vocals, rhythm guitar
about: Creedence Clearwater Revival's second studio album was recorded in Hollywood in late 1968 and released by Fantasy in January 1969. Produced by John Fogerty, it contains Born on the Bayou and Proud Mary, the band's breakthrough single, and climbed to No. 7 on the Billboard 200.

title: Jazz Erotica
label: HiFi Records
personnel: Bill Holman – baritone saxophone Frank Rosolino – trombone
Conte Candoli – trumpet Ed Leddy – trumpet

tracks.t: The Things You Did Last Summer

about: A West Coast jazz session co-led by tenor saxophonist Richie Kamuca and baritone saxophonist Bill Holman, recorded in May 1957 for HiFi Records with players such as Conte Candoli, Frank Rosolino and Vince Guaraldi. It was later reissued without its nude cover painting as West Coast Jazz in Hifi.

title: Little Creatures
label: Sire Records
personnel: David Byrne – guitar, vocals Chris Frantz – drums
Jerry Harrison – keyboards, guitar, backing vocals Tina Weymouth – bass guitar, backing vocals
about: Talking Heads' sixth studio album, self-produced and released in June 1985, swapped the dense polyrhythms of earlier records for compact, roots-tinged pop songs. Singles such as Road to Nowhere and And She Was helped make it one of the band's best sellers, certified double platinum in the US.

title: A Fantasy Love Affair
label: Drive Records

tracks.t: Do Ya Wanna Get Funky With Me / Burning Love Breakdown
It's True What They Say About Love

about: Peter Brown's debut album, produced by Cory Wade for the Miami label Drive, featured the disco hits Do Ya Wanna Get Funky with Me and Dance with Me. It went into the top twenty of the Billboard pop albums chart and the top ten of the R&B albums list.

title: Later That Day...
label: Real People
personnel: Lyrics Born – Tsutomu "Tom" Shimura (fka Asia Born). Joyo Velarde. Lateef (the Truthsayer) – Lateef Daumont
about: The first solo studio album by Bay Area rapper Lyrics Born, released on Quannum Projects in 2003. Framed loosely as a single day in his life, it mixes funk and soul-flavored production, partly by Cut Chemist, with guests including Gift of Gab and Joyo Velarde, and includes the single Callin' Out.

title: Say It Live and Loud - 08.26.68 Live in Dallas
label: Republic Records
personnel: Alfred "Pee Wee" Ellis – leader, alto saxophone, organ
St-Clair Pinckney – tenor saxophone, baritone saxophone
Maceo Parker, Jr. – tenor saxophone, soloist, mc

tracks.t: Introduction To Say It Loud - I'm Black And I'm Proud
Say It Loud - I'm Black And I'm Proud
I Guess I'll Have To Cry, Cry, Cry
Papa's Got A Brand New Bag
I Can't Stand Myself (When You Touch Me)
Say It Loud, I'm Black And I'm Proud

about: An archival concert recording of James Brown and his band at Dallas Memorial Auditorium on 26 August 1968, issued by PolyGram three decades later. It captures an early live performance of Say It Loud – I'm Black and I'm Proud, and a fuller vinyl edition followed for its 50th anniversary in 2018.

title: Don't Call Me John
label: ABB Records
about: The debut EP from Brooklyn-born, Bay Area-based rapper and producer Superstar Quamallah, released in 1999 on ABB Records during the West Coast independent hip-hop boom of the late 1990s.

title: Aretha in Paris
label: Atlantic Records

tracks.t: Don't Let Me Lose This Dream
(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman
Dr. Feelgood (Love Is A Serious Business)
Since You've Been Gone (Sweet Sweet Baby)
I Never Loved A Man (The Way I Love You)

about: Aretha Franklin's first live album for Atlantic, recorded at the Olympia in Paris in May 1968 and produced by Jerry Wexler. Released that autumn, it captured her touring band at the height of her late-1960s success and reached No. 2 on the R&B albums chart and No. 13 on the Billboard 200.

title: Urban Renewal
label: Warner Bros Records
personnel: Lenny Pickett - clarinet, bass. clarinet, alto flute, baritone, tenor & soprano saxophones Chester D

about: Tower of Power's fifth studio album was recorded at the Record Plant in Sausalito and released by Warner Bros. in early 1975. It was the final record with lead singer Lenny Williams, included the R&B singles Willing to Learn and Only So Much Oil in the Ground, and reached No. 22 on the pop chart.

title: Chic
label: Atlantic Records
about: Chic's debut album, produced by Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards and released on Atlantic in late 1977, launched the band with the hit Dance, Dance, Dance (Yowsah, Yowsah, Yowsah) and the follow-up Everybody Dance. Both singles topped the US club chart, and the album was certified gold.

about: Willie Nelson's 70th solo studio album, produced by Buddy Cannon for Legacy Recordings, was pushed from April to July 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It pairs a few new originals with covers, ending with Charles Aznavour's Yesterday When I Was Young, and reached the top five of Billboard's country albums chart.

label: Legacy Records

about: Willie Nelson's 66th solo studio album, produced by Buddy Cannon and released by Legacy in April 2017, reflects on aging and mortality. The title track features one of Leon Russell's final recordings, and the album opened at No. 1 on Billboard's Top Country Albums chart and No. 10 on the Billboard 200.

about: Amii Stewart's debut studio album, produced by Barry Leng and released in 1979 (titled Amii Stewart in the UK), was built around her disco reworking of Eddie Floyd's Knock on Wood, which topped the US singles chart. It also included a disco version of Light My Fire and went gold in the US.

about: The self-titled debut by Village People, created by producers Jacques Morali and Henri Belolo for Casablanca in 1977. Its four lengthy disco tracks name-check gay hotspots such as San Francisco and Fire Island, and it was eventually certified gold in the US.

about: Millie Jackson's self-titled debut, released on Spring Records in 1972 and produced by Raeford Gerald, introduced the soul singer with the R&B hits Ask Me What You Want and My Man, a Sweet Man, both of which reached the soul top ten.

about: An easy-listening guitar album by session guitarist Tony Mottola, released in 1968 on Enoch Light's audiophile label Project 3. It presents mostly familiar pop and standard tunes in inventive arrangements played by top New York studio musicians.

about: A 2017 vinyl compilation of early Nina Simone material issued by the European reissue label Jazz Wax. It gathers live tracks from Atlantic City in 1956 and Chicago in 1960 alongside orchestral studio sides recorded in New York between 1959 and 1961, originally released as singles.

about: A double live album by Peter Frampton, assembled from 1975 concerts mostly at San Francisco's Winterland Ballroom and released by A&M in January 1976. It spent ten weeks at No. 1, became the top-selling album of 1976 and produced the hits Show Me the Way, Baby, I Love Your Way and Do You Feel Like We Do.

about: A spoken-word album on which poet Sarah Webster Fabio reads her work over funk and jazz backing played by her children's band, Don't Fight the Feeling. First issued by Folkways in 1976, it was later reissued on vinyl by Smithsonian Folkways and is seen as a forerunner of poetry set to groove-based music.

title: Fancy Free
label: Blue Note Records / VMP
personnel: Julian Priester – trombone Frank Foster – tenor and soprano saxophone Duke Pearson – electric piano
about: Donald Byrd's Blue Note album recorded at Van Gelder Studio in mid-1969 and produced by Duke Pearson. Using a large ensemble with extra percussion and Pearson on electric piano, it marked the trumpeter's first step toward the groove-based jazz-funk that defined his work in the 1970s.
